items.evidence: horizon-items/src/items.rs LootContext (line numbers verified fresh in the 1.21.10 tree): (1) condition() (line 1986) reads the kind ONLY from o.get("type") (line 1991) — no dual-form read (contrast the 26.2 tree, items.rs:2090); 1.21.10's data uses the "condition" key throughout (1,536 occurrences, 0 type-keyed), so every object condition's kind is "" and the match falls to _ => false. conditions() (line 2112) DOES consult the plural "conditions" array, but every element fails; nested conditions fail the same way (inverted's term, any_of/all_of's terms). (2) evaluate() applies pool["modifier"]/table["modifier"] (lines 1873-1874), expand() pushes e["modifier"] (line 2146, applied by choose()), nested() applies entry["modifier"] (line 2287) — 1.21.10's data has ZERO "modifier" keys and puts functions in "functions" arrays (950: 931 entry/10 pool/9 table), so no function ever runs; modifiers()'s own dual-form discriminator read (f["type"].or(f["function"]), line 2311) is dead code. No normalisation in the load path (loot.rs load_dir lines 773-790 parses files straight into the shared map). Impact over all 1,320 tables: 1,186 carry >=1 condition or >=1 function — blocks 1,050/1,083 (1,021 with a condition, 225 with a function), entities 58/104, chests 54/56, gameplay 6/26, dispensers 3/3, equipment 3/3, spawners 3/5, shearing 3/22, harvest 2/3, archaeology 1/6, carve 1/1, charged_creeper 1/6, pots 1/1, brush 0/1; only 134 tables roll correctly. Survival path traced: Game::block_loot_at (game.rs:3694) -> block_drops_by_player (items.rs:1562) -> block_drops_raw (items.rs:1623) -> ctx.evaluate (items.rs:1660/1674) — every conditioned pool/entry is dropped, so survival block-breaking drops nothing from conditioned tables (same symptom the owner confirmed in-game for 1.21.7). /loot routes all table types through this engine too (loot_table_for_command items.rs:1688; entity_drops_for_command / entity_drops_with_target items.rs:1793/1805). Post-fix residual recorded here: modifiers() has 12 arms and is missing 7 of the 19 function kinds in the data (copy_components 71 block tables, furnace_smelt 16 entity, set_enchantments 4, set_stew_effect 3, exploration_map 3, set_ominous_bottle_amplifier 3, set_instrument 1 — union 101 tables, verified disjoint fresh from the jar data), and expand() (line 2127) has no minecraft:tag arm (default _ => false, line 2219; the single tag entry, entities/creeper.json); union + tag = 102 tables, exactly the 26.2 run's B12-G01 count. The 26.2 tree reads ["functions"] + dual-form discriminators (items.rs:1969-1970/2090/2246/2387, loot.rs:1042/2126/2164) — the 26.2 playtest fixes were never carried to 1.21.10.

items.evidence: horizon-world/src/loot.rs is written for the 26.3 loot format throughout (line numbers verified fresh): condition() (line 1368) reads only c["type"] (line 1377) while 1.21.10's 1,536 conditions all use the "condition" key; modify() (line 1478) consults singular m["condition"] only (line 1488) while 1.21.10's 184 function-level condition lists are plural "conditions"; run() (line 1512) reads only f["type"] (line 1514) while 1.21.10's 1,362 functions all use the "function" key (default _ => {}, line 1937); table_raw() (line 2021) checks singular pool["condition"] (line 2028) and applies pool/table["modifier"] (lines 2039/2026) while 1.21.10 has 952 plural pool "conditions" arrays (including 6 nested inside an entry's value, in equipment/trial_chamber.json) and 0 "modifier" keys; expand() (line 2080) checks singular entry["condition"] (line 2081) while 1.21.10's 245 entry lists are plural, so every entry passes its gate; create() (line 2131) applies entry["modifier"] (line 2133); the minecraft:tag arm reads entry["items"] (lines 2110/2146) while 1.21.10's tag entry uses the "name" field (minecraft:creeper_drop_music_discs) — contrast the 26.2 tree's tag_entry_items (loot.rs:1042). Precision: the file's only f["functions"] read (line 1516) is inside the minecraft:sequence arm of run(), itself unreachable because the discriminator at 1514 reads type only, and minecraft:sequence is not among the 19 function kinds in the data. run() has 26 arms covering 15 of the 19 function kinds, missing only the block-only kinds apply_bonus/copy_components/copy_state/explosion_decay (engine-scope boundary, not a defect: loot.rs never serves block tables). Demonstrated LIVE with the loot_fill example against the real prepared data (7 tables x seeds 1-5, evidence/loot_fill.txt, 148 lines): every stack count 1 (set_count never runs); the gated music_disc_lava_chicken on ALL 5 zombie seeds; blocks/stone -> minecraft:stone and blocks/diamond_ore -> minecraft:diamond_ore on all 5 seeds (silk-touch alternative wins unconditionally); entities/creeper -> gunpowder x1 only (tag entry never expands, set_count never applies); no enchantments anywhere. Affects entity drops, chest/container loot, fishing, trial spawners and vaults. 0 additional gap checks: these tables are already counted under items.rs (B12-G01).

items.evidence: The 1.21.10 jar ships ZERO supports_* block tags and only two fluid tags (lava, water); no synthesize_legacy_support_tags code exists in the 1.21.10 tree (the 1.21.7 tree's fix was never carried). Eleven runtime tag reads point at 26.x names and resolve to EMPTY sets in BOTH survival implementations: block_survival.rs tag_states/fluid_tag (missing keys yield empty sets, lines 482-497): supports_cocoa (:593), supports_mangrove_propagule (:600), supports_hanging_mangrove_propagule (:601), supports_frogspawn (:609 block + :619 fluid), supports_sugar_cane (:611), supports_sugar_cane_adjacently (:612 block + :620 fluid); horizon-prepare/src/survival.rs export table -> TagBelow rules (bound_tags, :573-576): supports_azalea (:76), supports_nether_sprouts (:85), supports_nether_wart (:87); level/survive.rs reads the same empty sets via Tags::resolve (level/data.rs:399-401, unwrap_or_default): cocoa :150, hanging mangrove :256, sugar cane :341/:348-349, azalea :403, mangrove :430, nether sprouts :432, nether wart :433, frogspawn :477-478. Every affected block's vanilla 1.21.10 form was javap-verified on the client-named jar and uses NO supports_* tag: SugarCane = #dirt/#sand below + water adjacent; Cocoa = #jungle_logs; MangrovePropagule = SaplingBlock.mayPlaceOn or clay, hanging = mangrove leaves above; Frogspawn = fluid below WATER + above EMPTY; Azalea = clay or VegetationBlock.mayPlaceOn; NetherSprouts = #nylium or soul soil or VegetationBlock.mayPlaceOn; NetherWart = soul sand only. Consequence: 7 block types can never survive on valid ground (e.g. Rule::SugarCane, block_survival.rs:1096-1122, returns false when the block below is not in the empty set). 11 gap checks: the 11 unique tag names actually read (9 block + 2 fluid). The remaining supports_* fields in the level Tags struct (supports_cactus/wither_rose/lily_pad/chorus_plant, fluid supports_lily_pad) have no gameplay readers — dead fields, uncounted.
items.method: tag census (jar vs prepared) + runtime tag-read audit + javap on the 7 owning block classes

items.evidence: horizon-client-render/src/assets.rs, Assets::load (line 186) REQUIRES three tags from block-tags.json with hard errors: minecraft:blocks_motion_in_heightmap (:212-216, "missing motion tag"), minecraft:blocks_motion_in_heightmap_no_leaves (:217-221, "missing no-leaves motion tag"), minecraft:blocks_fluid_flow (:224-229, "missing fluid flow tag"). None exists in 1.21.10: the jar's 203 block tags contain no blocks_motion* or blocks_fluid_flow file, and the prepared block-tags.json (203/203 exact-equal to the jar) contains none either. No synthesis or derivation exists anywhere in the 1.21.10 tree (TagDefinitions::build, worldgen/tags.rs:149, does not synthesise them; no horizon-prepare step writes them). The load therefore fails with "missing motion tag" before the game can start — the exact crash the 1.21.7 port hit on its first laptop launch (Nov 21), fixed there by deriving the sets from block data (versions/1.21.7/.../assets.rs:212-283: blocks_fluid_flow: blocks_motion.into()); that fix was never carried to the 1.21.10 tree. 3 gap checks: the three hard-required tag reads. May overlap Batch 3's startup-blocker item (B3-G22-equivalent) — flagged for the coordinator to fold, not to double-count.

systemic_note: The prepared data is faithful — all 5,058 data-driven files byte-identical to the 1.21.10 jar, block-tags.json byte-faithful too. Every defect is code reading the 26.x form of a format 1.21.10 writes differently and failing silently — the same bug class as the 1.21.7 pilot's 26.x-tag findings (G1/G3/G5/G6), now in three places at once: (1) loot keys — 1.21.10 writes the old forms (condition/function discriminators, plural conditions arrays, functions arrays, tag-entry name) while both engines read the 26.3 forms (type, modifier, singular condition, tag items), and the 26.2 playtest fixes that taught the engines both forms were never carried to the 1.21.10 tree; (2) survival tags — 1.21.10 has no supports_* tags at all (vanilla uses native tags and hardcoded blocks), the port adapted most checks to those native forms but left eleven reads pointing at 26.x names, and every tag lookup defaults missing tags to empty instead of failing loudly; (3) motion/fluid-flow tags — the asset loader demands three 26.x-only tags with hard errors, and 1.21.7's derivation fix was never carried, so the 1.21.10 client fails at the same startup point 1.21.7 did before its fix. The port DOES get the 1.21.10 forms right where it was written for them (specials hardcoded to the bare form, per-type cooking defaults, transmute bounds, recipe/advancement/enchantment/damage loaders); the defects are the places where 26.3-base code survived the port untouched.
